cohort: The study included 631 women aged > 15 years with Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) recruited from seven centers in India.
finding: The study highlights that Systemic lupus erythematosus significantly impacts pregnancy, both before and after disease onset, leading to reduced pregnancies and live births, and increased rates of pregnancy loss, stillbirths, and abortions, along with complications like hypertension and pre-eclampsia.
